[[Providence Park|Multnomah Stadium]] }} {{1961 Western college football independents records}} The '''1961 Oregon State Beavers football team''' represented [[Oregon State University]] as an independent during the [[1961 college football season]]. Led by seventh-year head coach [[Tommy Prothro]], the Beavers ended their third season as an [[Independent (college sports)|independent]] with five wins and five losses, and outscored their opponents 198 to 192. Four home games were played on campus at [[Parker Stadium]] in [[Corvallis, Oregon|Corvallis]] with one at [[Multnomah Stadium]] in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]]. Prior to this season, the university's current title, Oregon State University, was adopted by a legislative act signed into law by [[List of governors of Oregon|Governor]] [[Mark Hatfield]] on March 6, 1961, and became effective in the summer.{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=XP9VAAAAIBAJ&sjid=0uIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=2154%2C807741 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |agency=Associated Press |title=OSU measure signed by Gov.
